membership.description: The publication explicitly identifies the taxon within the retained group or stage union.
The closest represented taxonomic or ecological analogue is used, with the source membership and habitat mismatch retained.
The taxon unambiguously meets the source group definition and its represented stage union.
An authoritative synonym connects the catch label to a taxon explicitly named in the source.
The taxon has source support but its habitat or life stage only partly fits the modeled compartment.
A broad reporting category is approximated by a represented group set despite unknown composition or unrepresented members.
Source definitions support a candidate group union, while the exact taxonomic, trophic or stage boundary requires an assumption.
Documented ecology supports an extension to a group whose source list does not explicitly name the taxon.
Membership is extended from source-listed representatives to related small pelagic taxa.
No defensible represented taxonomic or feeding analogue can be established.

allocation.description: Historical source-model landings proportions proxy the regional catch composition across years and catch bases; the existing skipjack infant-zero assumption is retained.
Complete model biomass proportions supply the allocation when raw catches are incomplete, assuming transferable caught composition and catchability.
The entire taxon is assigned to its sole eligible group; no allocation split is required.
No eligible represented compartment supports a defensible numerical allocation.

very_low.reason: Coastal, reef, demersal or benthopelagic fish lack explicit membership. Epi fish and its small stage are weak analogues with habitat, feeding and adult-stage mismatches. Complete source biomass proxies catch composition after incomplete raw catches; the assumption transfers across taxa, years and catch bases.

Shark pools approximate broader cartilaginous-fish reporting that includes unrepresented rays and chimaeras. Unknown composition and transfer of historical model landings proportions limit the decision.

Pelagic crustacean and migratory-forage pools approximate reporting that also includes benthic shrimps, crabs or lobsters. Habitat and composition mismatches remain; complete model biomass proxies regional caught composition after incomplete raw catches.

Shark pools approximate a reporting category that also includes unrepresented rays and skates. Their unknown contribution and transfer of historical model landings proportions limit the decision. Chimaeras are outside this label.

The complete source-defined bony-fish union is used, including named stages and fish-bearing mixed forage pools. Unknown residual composition and invertebrates within mixed-pool biomass limit membership. Incomplete raw catches require full model-biomass proportions, assumed transferable across 1950–2019 and all catch bases.

The category includes unrepresented benthic molluscs and represented pelagic molluscs. Dedicated and mixed mollusc-bearing forage pools form a weak composite, weighted by complete model biomass after incomplete raw catches.

Benthic octopuses are approximated by surface-pelagic Argonautidae in Epi mollusc and its small stage. The benthic/pelagic mismatch is substantial; incomplete raw catches require a model-biomass composition and catchability assumption.

Epi fish and its small stage are a weak proxy for an unmeasured demersal-fish mixture, with omitted species and habitat mismatches. Complete model biomass proxies catch composition after incomplete raw catches.

Named tuna stages and residual scombrid pools approximate an unknown mix of mackerels, tunas and bonitos, including unlisted taxa. Complete model biomass proxies the family catch mix after incomplete raw catches.

The bigeye adult/small pair is a weak Thunnus analogue for unlisted albacore and bluefin. Species, temperature and maturity thresholds differ. Historical bigeye landings proportions are transferred to the target taxa and all years/bases.

uncertainty: Overall confidence follows the weaker membership or allocation component. Each rule percentage is the share of independent simple-chain PPR for taxa using that rule. Bivalvia and Echinodermata remain unresolved because this pelagic model has no defensible corresponding feeding or taxonomic compartment; both have zero 2019 landings.
missing_inputs_note: 25 catch labels lack a saved TL or simple-chain coefficient; all have zero 2019 landings and therefore contribute zero annual PPR. No positive-catch PPR contribution is unknown.
review_scope: Current adopted mappings and confidence retained after full-universe source/evidence checks; no regional inputs or group SPPR changed.
